approach: Query IA by authors the Library already validates as tier-1, instead of by IA subject tags. tier_queries.sql applies its subject patterns to Gutenberg's LoC-derived subjects, which are curated; IA's are user-supplied folksonomy, which is why the same patterns returned family letters.

why.finding: IA's rights field is populated on a narrow and unrepresentative slice. 1 of 2,015 Twain texts carries rights:"public domain" — not because the others are in copyright, but because the field is rarely set. The contract makes that field mandatory, so it excludes almost the entire relevant corpus.

but_the_filter_is_protective.note: printdisabled and inlibrary are the controlled-digital-lending collections the contract excludes explicitly after Hachette v. IA. Loosening the rights filter to reach volume would pull borrow-only material into scope. The filter is not merely conservative — it is the thing keeping ingestion legal.

conclusion: Gap 2 is not blocked on query craft. It is blocked on a genuine tension: IA's rights metadata is too sparse to find the tier-1 corpus, and the alternative signals available (collection membership, absent copyright status) are exactly the ones that indicate borrow-only material. Resolving it means either accepting a tiny high-confidence corpus, or a rights determination I am not qualified to make.
